- When sentiment is negative in the recent history, reduce forecasted prices by 2–5% to account for bearish momentum.  
- If model forecast spikes sharply after a recent high, cap the next 3–5 days’ forecast at 10–15% below the peak to avoid overshoot.  
- If sentiment alternates between positive and negative, favor mean reversion in the 10–15 day horizon — forecast should trend toward historical average of last 10–12 days.  
- When sentiment is consistently positive over 5+ days, model tends to overestimate — apply a 3–7% downward adjustment to the 30-day forecast.  
- If true outcome shows a sharp drop after a forecast peak, assume sentiment shift occurred — adjust next forecast downward by 5–10% to reflect new market sentiment.  
- For 30-day forecasts, if true outcome is consistently below 65% of historical mean, reduce forecast by 5–10% to avoid overconfidence in upward bias.
